summary: Live chances (Leo, 31 Oct 2026): own switch kib-live-chances, off by default; with the kick screen (on by default) letting go sets the timing, then the game's normal kick screen picks where on the ball.
body:
Leo, 31 Oct 2026: "i meant normal kick screen, the second part of the aiming and kicking bit, not this new weird thing" (a small strip along the pitch was built first and removed).

Saved per phone in localStorage `kib-live-chances` ({on, strike, dials}); shown in Settings → Match (admins, `LiveChancesSettings`) and Settings → Updates. Off = the old path untouched.

On: open-play ground chances hand over before the build-up's last pass arrives (`planFromLead`; no build-up = `planMadeUp`); CanvasMatch steps it (`stepLive`). Kick screen on: the release is the moment you meet it; out of reach = fresh air at once; in reach, `lv.armed` keeps that ball and speed, the pass stops (`stepLive` returns while armed), the normal ContactBall opens, and its tap goes to `liveTapStrike` → `readSwing(…, tap)` (the tap's cx/cy moved by the timing). Off: the release reads the swing directly. The strike goes through `handleContact` → `launch`. 3D: the frame's `grabAt`; a press on the spot is never a team-mate order.

Test page `/star-live-chances-dev`; tests `tests/star/liveChance.mts`; drivers `scripts/film/live/`.

summary: Live chances first touch (Leo, 1 Nov 2026): a quick flick from the ring is ONE touch; the keeper rushes in one-on-ones and either smothers it or is beaten.
body:
Leo's picks (31 Oct 2026): quick flick, keeper rushes, stays live, every live chance.

A release quicker than TOUCH.maxMs (240 ms) and longer than TOUCH.minSwipe (4.5% of the pitch's height) is a touch in the flick's direction (`isTouchFlick`, CanvasMatch onPointerUp → `liveTouch`); its length is the weight. It is timed like a strike (`readTouch`). The ball then rolls (`planAfterTouch`, plan.roll), you run onto it (`runnerAt`), the ring moves to where you catch it, then you carry it at your feet for up to TOUCH.holdS (2.5 s real) before CLOSED DOWN.

In one_on_one / through_ball the keeper rushes (`keeperRushes`, `rushTarget`, 4.4–6.0 m/s by rating) and, at the touch, `keeperVsTouch` decides: he reaches it before you (SAVED, outcome "caught") or he is beaten (low dive held TOUCH.downS, then back to his line). While he rushes or reacts, stepKeeper/brainAim are skipped for him (stepLiveMen moves him). Balance: scripts/film/live/touchbalance.mts. Browser driver: scripts/film/live/touchcheck.mjs.

summary: Live chances: the player's stats set the skill (technique, pace, vision, power; liveDialsFor), and everyone moves (defenders close down/cover/chase the touch, team-mates carry on their runs).
body:
Leo, 1 Nov 2026: "anything skill related should be related to levels … decided by the player's stats" and "add moving everything to live chances". His picks: defenders + team-mates; the stats plan as below; the sliders on the test page only.

Stats (40 floor, 95 top; tired legs count; `liveSkillsNow` in CanvasMatch): technique → clean zone 0.22–0.50 m, early reach 0.8–1.3 m, touch error ×1.35–×0.6 (`touchErrorScale`); pace → late reach 0.6–1.1 m and the run after a touch (`touchChaseSpeed`); vision → time for the pass 1.3–2.3 s and slow motion near you ×0.72–×0.40; power → the strike (launch). Game Settings keep only the two switches; the test page has stats sliders, presets and by-hand dials (`setLiveTest({stats, manual})`).

Movement (`stepLiveMen`, `DEF`): once the build-up has played out (or after your touch), defenders within 16 m move at 5.6 m/s × their speed: the nearest presses to 1.4 m short of the ball, the rest go goal-side (`defenderTarget`); after a touch the nearest two race for it (`keeperVsTouch` with DEF.reachM) and the first there before you wins it (TACKLED), and on the ball a defender within 0.85 m takes it. Team-mates carry on their build-up runs at 85%, easing off over 1.6 s.

summary: Match free kicks: a ball into the very top corner beats the keeper about 4 in 5 (FREE_KICK.corner, cornerness); was 11% against a 92 keeper.
body:
Leo, 1 Nov 2026: "full power perfect top corner … 100% the keeper saves it." Cause: at 17–19 m/s a top keeper (react 0.08 s) got across and his 2.7 m reach covered the corner; the top-corner reach cut was off for match free kicks.

Fix: `cornerness(ball)` (0..1, from where it will cross: full within cornerEdge[0] of a post and above cornerZ[0], none past cornerEdge[1] / below cornerZ[1]). The keeper aims cornerShortM × cornerness short of it and his reach is cut by cornerCut × cornerness. Drill free kicks unchanged (FREE_KICK_DRILL corner off).

Measured (scripts/fk/cornerFk.mts, 99/99 taker, every aim/power/curl/lift, real engine + match setup): very top corner 11% → 79% vs 80/92/95 keepers; realism test ordinary 10% → 16% (bound raised to 18%), specialist 25%. A general slow-down or a worse start position made ordinary kicks up to 36% without helping the corner; not used.

Replaces FACT-TEAM-005 (five bots); what those five post, and when, is unchanged (lib/teamRoom/botsServer.ts). One list: BOTS in lib/teamRoom/patchBot.ts; the @ names: AT_BOTS in lib/teamRoom/extras.ts ("@Harry bot" is the bot, never Harry). Typing @ suggests bots under people. A bot's answer is a row in team_bot_posts with meta.kind "reply", meta.reply_to (the thread), meta.ask (the asking message), meta.by: one per bot per ask. A bot's row is never read as a question, so a bot never answers a bot; a message older than 10 minutes is never answered. Trigger: the asker's browser posts { ask: id } to /api/admin/team/bots the moment the message is sent (messages are written straight from the browser, so no server route sees them); the 15-minute timer (/api/cron/patch-bot) and an admin opening an admin page sweep for a missed one. The AI is given no tools: the only rows written are the bot's own reply and the month's running total. Key: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, server only (lib/teamRoom/claudeClient.ts), never in code, a browser or a log; unset = the page says "not switched on yet: one Vercel setting" and an @ gets that line. Cap: each reply's cost is worked out from the token counts the AI service returns and kept on the reply row (meta.usage); a running-total row (bot "claude-tally") covers rows the table has dropped (it keeps 500); the larger of the two counts; each dollar is counted as a pound. At the cap: "I've hit this month's limit", no AI call. Also 1 answer per person per 20 seconds, 60 a day, admins only. It is shown the thread, the channel's last 30 messages, up to 3 Brain notes (lib/teamRoom/brainBundle.json, made at build by scripts/brain/bundle-for-site.mjs) and the 5 newest patch notes; the reply names the Brain codes it was given or says "no note yet". A person's own key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_HARRY, _MIKEY, _LEO) gives that person's bot its own cap. No SQL.

summary: Neither Harry nor Mikey writes code: english only, no coder words.
Answer shape: key point, key number, key change; no preamble, no restating the request, no praise.
Write about 80% of the way to ASD-STE100: short sentences (20-25 words at most), active voice, no coder words.
Any stat, rate or rule with conditions gets a picture, but only where a picture is clearer than one plain line.
Every claim carries a number, or admits it has none; always give the before alongside the after.
Say whether you saw it, measured it, or reasoned it.
Show, don't describe, anything with a size or a shape: render the options at real phone size (show-options agent).
Play it before claiming it works: a type-check and a green suite cannot see a frozen figure; use star-playtest.
Ask about the one ambiguous word; build the rest, then ask one question that can be answered in a word.
When Harry points at a picture, name it back in one line (which picture you are copying) before building.
Do not agree to be agreeable: before agreeing with a design call, find what argues against it.
SQL for a person to run goes out as an artifact page (each file's name, one line on what it does, a Copy all button and the full text), never as links; build it with scripts/supabase/sql-page.py.
body: Every time someone needs to run SQL in Supabase, publish one page with every file to run, in order. Each card: the file name, what it switches on, a Copy all button and the whole file. Make it with `python3 scripts/supabase/sql-page.py OUT.html "Title" <file> "what it does" ...` (a file can be `git:<ref>:<path>`). Never only a GitHub link. Check the live tables afterwards and say which now exist.

summary: Every Supabase request Claude makes starts with a plain-English header in the SQL (READ ONLY or CHANGES THE DATABASE, What, Why) and the same lines in chat before the Allow box; changes wait for a yes.

The Allow box shows only the raw request, so the SQL itself opens with `-- READ ONLY.` or `-- CHANGES THE DATABASE.`, then `What:` and `Why:` in plain words. Calls with no SQL (advisors, list tables) get the same three lines in chat just before. A change (apply_migration, insert, update, delete) also goes out first as an RUL-DAT-001 page and waits for Harry's yes.

summary: Everything goes on the admin page, always: every patch note and every update to one is shipped to the site and checked live; an update is marked (updatedAt + updateNote) so it shows UPDATED, moves to the front and is unread again.
body:
Leo, 24 Oct 2026: *"i never want patch notes kept to me and you on this chat!
EVERYTHING ON THE ADMIN PAGE ALWAYS! with progress updates and patch note
updates. also if u update an old patch notes then make sure its clear."*

- Every new patch note, and every change to one, goes to main with
  `node scripts/patch-notes/ship.mjs <v>` (`--update` for a change) the same
  turn it is made (PRO-TEAM-007). Progress bars go to the board
  (`scripts/post-status.mjs`) as the work moves.
- An update sets `updatedAt` (now) and a one-line `updateNote` saying what
  changed. The archive then tags it UPDATED, puts it first, and counts it
  unread again for everyone (read receipts are per update); the phone buzz
  says "Updated patch notes". `ship.mjs --update` refuses an update without them.
- "Live" is said only after checking it: Vercel's status for the merge
  commit, then the live site's own code carrying that commit (search the
  /star-dev chunks for the SHA). If it can't be checked, say so.

summary: Every patch note: author, real date and time, every update with time and where, its own number (no base shared with anyone's, search all branches), a menu name saying what it is about, and the one standard page; checked by rules.mjs.
body:
Applies to Harry's, Mikey's and Leo's notes alike. In lib/patchNotesData.ts a
note has "author", "publishedAt" (the real time, never a midnight guess), a
title "<Name>'s patch notes: <what it is about>", and "updates" (each { at,
where, note }); an update also sets updatedAt + updateNote and appends the
same line to "updates". A number is used once: "0.121" and "0.121h" may not
both exist; retired numbers (0.60-0.63, 0.103, 0.107-0.110) are never reused.
Every note has a page built from the standard (artifact-house-style:
tuning-plan-standard.html, clip-card.html, a "Check these" list). The checks
live in scripts/patch-notes/rules.mjs: tests/star/patchNoteRules.mts runs them
on every note and ship.mjs refuses a note that breaks one. Supersedes
RUL-TEAM-006.

summary: Leo's chats: start with a plan as progress bars (steps, time each, % done), update them and the admin board often; end every task with yes/no lines (works? patch notes made/updated? live on admin page? merged into the game?), then at most 5 lines; ask for every approval together at the start or end.
body:
At the start of a task: the steps as bars with a time for each (progress-update skill). While working: refresh the bars in chat and on the admin board (post-status.mjs) at each step. At the end, first the yes/no block:
- Works (seen how) — yes/no
- Patch notes made / updated — yes/no
- Patch notes live on the admin page — yes/no
- Merged into the game (live) — yes/no
Then at most 5 lines; anything longer goes in a closed <details> block if the surface shows one, else is left out. Permission prompts: gather what needs Leo's OK into one ask at the start or the end, never mid-task.

summary: A Team room bot never changes anything. A person's bot turns a bigger ask into a card only its owner can Accept; Accept adds one job to the owner's own to-do for their own Claude chat.
body: Harry, 13 Nov 2026: "if needed it can use my actual Claude. But it should maybe propose it rather than just do it. Obviously bots ask for permission before they change anything." A bigger ask = anything that needs a change to the game, files or database (a plain word rule, wantsChange in lib/teamRoom/claudeBot.ts), or the AI answering HANDOFF. The bot posts "This needs <Owner>'s Claude. Send it?" in the thread. Only the owner can press Accept or Decline (the site checks who is signed in). Accept: exactly one row in the owner's to-do ("🤖 For my Claude: …", made in the owner's name by the owner's own press) and the text for their Claude chat kept on the card (who asked what, the thread, its link, "wait for my yes before changing anything"). A website cannot reach into anyone's Claude account: the job waits until the owner's own chat takes it, by Copy for my Claude, or by the chat hook scripts/hooks/bot-jobs-hook.mjs (the pipe recordings already use; written, not switched on until a person adds it to .claude/settings.json). The chat's reply comes back once through scripts/team-room/bot-job-done.mjs and shows in the thread as "<Owner>'s Claude". A person's bot is labelled "<Name> bot", never speaks as the person, and never accepts a task or approves anything for them. Its settings (on/off, How I should answer, channels, hand on: ask or never) are its owner's alone. Build-your-own bots: not built.

summary: Decide, don't toggle, EXCEPT skins: a whole-UI skin (e.g. Glass stadium) may be a Settings choice; gameplay and single-feature looks still get no New/Old row.
body:
Replaces RUL-UI-001. Harry, 1 Nov 2026: "on RUL-UI-001, toggles for skins are okay."

- **Skins may be toggles.** A skin restyles the whole UI (buttons, cards, bars,
  background) over the same layout and rules. It can sit in Settings → UI as a
  player choice. First one: Glass stadium, the default (1 Nov 2026).
- **Everything else is unchanged from RUL-UI-001.** A gameplay change or a new
  look for one feature is built as THE game, with no "New | Old" row. Old
  versions live in git. Anything still being judged goes on a test/dev page.
